pass_a_gloss:
The creation is in Christ, because a new root has been laid. And a second Adam has come. And not like the first Adam, who was the cause of wrath and aversion from above to those who came from him, but rather a provider and giver of intimacy with God through sanctification and incorruptibility and righteousness in faith. These things Paul explains to us through the preceding statement. For he says that sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, and thus death passed to all men because all sinned. For death entered through sin in the first-formed man and in the beginning of the genus, and then the whole genus was divided. But also the serpent, the finder of sin, having prevailed in Adam in the ways of wickedness, has worked ruin on human thought. For all have turned away and have become worthless. Having become such from the face of the all-holy God, because the human mind has been carefully placed on evil things from youth, we live an irrational life. And death, having prevailed, has swallowed, as the prophet says, and Hades has widened its soul and opened its mouth so as not to leave anything, since we have become imitators of the transgression in Adam, according to which all sinned, and we have been handed over to the same justice. But the earth under heaven has not remained unconquered, for sin has been taken away, Satan has fallen, and death has been abolished. For until the law, sin was in the world.

The law through Moses was a rebuke of the weakness of those who sinned, not a release from sin; it worked more wrath; for it was necessary for those who transgressed the appointed laws to suffer just punishments; where there was transgression, there was also sin; if sin is a cause of death, it is necessary to say that death also arises from it; the law was in the world until sin was spoken of; for as long as the law was in effect, the crimes of transgression were being held against those who sinned; when the law ceased, the writing of transgressions also ceased; when sin ceased, death also ceased; but death reigned from Adam to Moses; if this is so, how can one say that death ruled over those on earth before the law, for even if some were not liable for transgressions of the law because it had not been given, they still suffered corruption like Adam's transgression; it is as if one would say that death ran its course according to the likeness of Adam's transgression, affecting all his descendants, just like a plant that has been damaged at its root, so that all its branches must wither
pass_b_english: The creation is rooted in Christ because a new foundation has been laid, and a second Adam has come.
This second Adam provides a means of intimacy with God through sanctification, incorruptibility, and righteousness that comes from faith.
Paul explains this concept to us through his writings, stating that sin entered the world through one man, and death followed as a result of sin (Romans 5:12).
Consequently, death spread to all humanity because all people have sinned.
As it is written, 'For all have turned away'.
This is evident in the fact that death entered the world through the first man, and subsequently, the entire human race was affected.
Having become such from the face of the all-holy God, because the human mind has been carefully placed on evil things from youth, we live a life that is contrary to God's will.
The serpent, who introduced sin, prevailed in Adam and corrupted human thought, leading people away from God.
As a result, humanity has become worthless, for all have turned away and have become worthless.
However, through Christ, sin has been taken away, Satan has been defeated, and death has been abolished.
Prior to the law, sin was present in the world.
The law given through Moses served as a rebuke to the weakness of those who sinned, rather than a release from sin.
It was not a remedy for sin, but it actually worked to increase wrath.
For it was necessary for those who transgressed the laws appointed by the law to suffer just punishments.
Where there was transgression, sin was also present.
If sin is a cause of death, then it is necessary to say that death also arises from it.
The law was in effect in the world until sin was spoken of.
As long as the law was in effect, the crimes of transgression were being held against those who sinned.
When the law ceased, the writing of transgressions also ceased.
When sin ceased, death also ceased.
However, death reigned from Adam to Moses.
But if this is the case, how can one say that death ruled over those on earth before the law?
For even if some were not liable for transgressions of the law because it had not been given, they still suffered corruption like Adam's transgression.

It is as if one would say that death ran its course according to the likeness of Adam's transgression, affecting all his descendants, just like a plant that has been damaged at its root, so that all its branches must wither.
